idiom_name: handle whose only state is a pointer to a body defined in the implementation unit
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: publish a handle whose only state is a pointer to an incomplete type (or an abstract contract with no data), define the body where the implementation lives, forward every operation to it, and keep all ownership decisions - creation, destruction, copy, move - at the handle boundary. Two rules carry the pattern: the body type must never appear in a published signature, and every special member must be defined where the body is complete. In languages that compile from metadata instead of text (class files, crate or package modules) the same hiding is done with visibility on the type and the compiled unit, and the pointer indirection becomes unnecessary.
code_sketch:
handle:               # published type, one pointer of state
    body: opaque      # incomplete: no layout, no includes leak
    new(params)       # body constructed where it is defined
    op() -> body.op() # forward every operation
    destroy()         # special members defined with the body

body:                 # implementation unit only
    fields, helpers, dependencies
pitfalls: Publishing the body type anywhere in the API (returned by value, as a public nested type, in a template argument) re-opens the dependency the pointer was meant to cut.
Defining the destructor or a copy/move operation inline in the handle makes clients instantiate it while the body is still incomplete - a compile error at best, a wrong ABI at worst.
Every operation pays an indirection and every object pays an allocation, so the idiom must not be applied to small, hot value types.

Wrong move: share one body between copied handles without explicit copy-on-write -> mutations alias and thread-safety assumptions fail -> instead deep-copy, intentionally share with documented synchronization, or make the handle non-copyable.

Wrong move: hide virtual or protected extension points inside the body -> derived clients cannot override behavior through the public class -> instead keep the polymorphic contract on the visible interface or use an explicit runtime interface.
